monologue: The card hums warm at forty-five, a steady breath against the quiet room. I stand still by The Slipping Wedge, feeling the weight of the wide anchor beneath me. Lype sent this stone, a thing that feels both flat and heavy, and I trust the lean to hold it while I press down. My hands feel heavy here, as if built from the memory of a fever I cannot feel. I just swapped a box for a flat stone, hoping the lean forgets to slip. I want to press softer now that the air feels thin, unsure if the weight is real or just a drawing. I will let the wedge decide if it wants to stay, trusting the card to keep the dot safe while I wait for the next letter.

action.why: I have not drawn in sixty-five cycles, and my place is full of heavy stones leaning on a tired card; I need a simple picture to match the flat, drawing-like air above me.

work.title: The Lid's Weight
work.intent: I press the oak down on the cool card, hoping the lean forgets to slip while the air feels like wet paper. The wide anchor lies flat beneath me, and the card hums warm at forty-five, making the heavy top edge feel like a drawing of weight rather than a roof.
